meta.what: What it takes to stay alive over days in Heihe: weather, rooms, fuel, water, food, illness. Each number has <key>_src (where it comes from) and <key>_basis: reported (the source gives it), derived (worked out from reported figures; the working is in the research file) or play (chosen so the game can be played).
meta.research: docs/research/living.md (cited below as living.md and a section number); docs/research/occupation.md

climate.mean_max_c_src: living.md 1a: Heihe (Aihui) station 50468, CMA normals 1991-2020, read through Wikipedia's climate box; Blagoveshchensk agrees within about 1 C
climate.min_hour_src: living.md 1e: January's coldest reading falls 05:00-08:00 Beijing time on 15 of 24 days (Blagoveshchensk 3-hourly observations)
climate.max_hour_src: living.md 1e: the warmest reading is about 14:00 on 20 of 24 January days
climate.departure_keep_src: living.md, Suggested game numbers: anomaly = 0.66 x yesterday's + normal(0, 3.8 C), fitted to 11 Januaries at Blagoveshchensk (raw lag-1 0.74, SD 4.1)
climate.departure_sd_c_src: the same fit: a fresh 3.8 C each day with 0.66 kept is a standing spread of 3.8 / sqrt(1 - 0.66^2) = 5.06 C. The fit's per-winter offset (SD 1.3 C) and wider range on cold days are not used yet

river.breakup_doy_src: living.md 2: ice drift starts 26 April on average (18 April - 10 May); not used before L5
river.freeze_doy_src: living.md 2: Chinese normal 18 November; not used before L5

building.central_heat_c_src: a heated flat held at the WHO healthy minimum (occupation.md); Chinese design temperatures run 18-24 C
building.cool_tau_h_src: living.md 3b: the building's heat-accumulation coefficient beta, 32-100 h for Soviet-era panel and brick blocks (AKH 1989 guideline, table 3); 60 h for a middle flat in a 1980s block
building.above_outdoor_c_src: living.md 3c: an unheated block with only its people's heat settles about 3 K above outdoors (from the measured Ryazan block, Armstrong et al. 2000); 8 K with cooking and electricity, which an occupied city without power does not have
building.broken_window_mul_src: living.md 3d: a whole window gone cuts the time constant to 0.15 of itself and the flat sits at outdoor +0.5 K; 1 + 5.67 = 1 / 0.15
building.open_door_mul_src: no source: an open street door lets in about as much as most of a window
building.basement_c_src: living.md 4: +5 C under a block at -25 C outside, bracketed by the Russian +2 C design minimum, a Kyiv shelter at +5 C and Beijing garages at 0-5 C. The drift towards 0 C after weeks without heat is not used yet
building.basement_tau_h_src: no source for a time constant: the ground holds a basement for days
building.stove_room_c_src: a stove fed steadily holds a room at room temperature; living.md 5d puts the need for an 18 m2 room at 15 C at 1.4 kW, well under a 4.5 kW stove
building.stove_tau_h_src: no source: a small room warms within the hour of lighting a stove

fuel.coal_unit_burn_h_src: living.md 5b, Suggested numbers: one unit is a 2 kg scoop (play); raw coal 20.9 MJ/kg at 50% stove efficiency is 2.9 kWh a kg, 2.1 h at the 1.4 kW a room needs; 2 kg is 4.1 h. The 50% efficiency has no source
fuel.wood_unit_burn_h_src: living.md 5b-5c: one unit is a chair's worth, 5 kg of wood at 14.7 MJ/kg and 50% efficiency, 10 kWh, about 7.3 h at 1.4 kW
fuel.furniture_ground_floor_src: a shop's counters and shelves, in chair-sized pieces; no source
fuel.furniture_home_extra_src: living.md 5c: four chairs (20 kg), a table (21 kg) and a wardrobe (93 kg) make about 134 kg, 25 chair-sized pieces with the 8 above
fuel.furniture_per_upper_floor_src: a flat's tables, chairs, shelves and doors above, in chair-sized pieces; no count
fuel.wood_per_piece_src: furniture is counted in chair-sized pieces
fuel.break_noise_m_src: no source: smashing furniture is heard in the street
fuel.melt_fuel_h_src: occupation.md: about 0.79 MJ to melt and boil a litre from -20 C snow; 2 L at 50% stove efficiency is 3.2 MJ, 0.63 h at 1.4 kW

body.water_loss_l_per_day_src: living.md 6a: a resting adult with no intake in a cold flat loses about 1.3 L a day (IOM net 1.05 L plus a higher minimum urine)
body.water_reserve_l_src: living.md 6a: collapse and delirium at about 10% of body weight, day 5 without water; 10% of 65 kg
body.thirst_collapse_hp_per_h_src: living.md 6a: death about day 8 (7-11), three days after collapse: 100 / 72 h
body.water_walk_mul_src: no source: breathing and sweating out in the cold when moving
body.food_reserve_kcal_src: living.md 6b: with water, collapse and serious illness come at about day 40 without food (Getaz 2012; Faintuch 2000); 40 days of 2,100 kcal. Marked weakness at about day 12, here the meter at 70
body.starve_hp_per_h_src: living.md 6b: death at about day 60 (46-73), twenty days after collapse: 100 / 480 h
body.food_item_kcal_src: a day's dry rations: bread, sausage, noodles
body.sleep_needs_mul_src: the water and food figures are whole days, sleep included
body.cold_comfort_c_src: set so the night's street rule holds (1 at -18 C): heat loss outdoors scales with (12 - T) / 30. The game cools a body outdoors faster than living.md 6c's estimates for a dressed adult (0 to -0.3 C an hour); kept for the night as designed
body.indoor_comfort_c_src: occupation.md: people lived for weeks in occupied Mariupol flats down to 3 C. living.md 6c: still or asleep at 9 C or below for over 2 h, about -0.1 C an hour; under-dressed, -0.3. Here a 0 C room costs about -0.05 C an hour, a -10 C room -0.3
body.illness_below_c_src: occupation.md, WHO Housing and Health Guidelines: 18 C healthy indoor minimum
body.illness_risk_per_c_src: living.md 6d: respiratory infection risk x 1.04 for each C below 18 C indoors, compounding (Makinen 2009 outdoor 4.3% per C; Mu 2017 about 2.4%)
body.illness_per_h_src: no source for how fast the meter fills: a week in a 5 C room makes you ill
body.chill_after_h_src: living.md 6d: after a soaking or chilling the risk is x 2.6 for the next 4-5 days (Johnson and Eccles 2005); a chilling here is a body below 35 C
body.illness_recover_per_h_src: no source: two days warm and fed take a bad cold away

shops.taken_by_morning_src: living.md 7: staples bought out on day 1, residents start looting on days 3-5, shelves empty by days 8-13; the share of all goods left at the end of days 1, 2, 3 and 7 is 0.45, 0.30, 0.15 and 0.05, so each morning takes 0.55, 1 - 0.30/0.45, 1 - 0.15/0.30, then about 0.24 a day to 0.05. The timing is reported, the fractions are play
shops.taken_after_src: no source: soldiers and the last scavengers take what is left
